tagline: The historic heart of Istanbul — Ottoman mosques, Byzantine walls, the Grand Bazaar, and neighbourhoods that have barely changed in centuries.

items.name: Vefa Bozacısı
items.description: A legendary Istanbul institution since 1876 — famous for boza (a fermented wheat drink) but also excellent Turkish coffee. The interior is unchanged for over a century.
items.tip: Try the boza with a sprinkle of cinnamon and roasted chickpeas. It tastes like nothing else in the world.

items.name: Grand Bazaar Café
items.description: Several traditional tea houses inside the Grand Bazaar where traders and shoppers rest. Order çay and watch the world go by.

items.name: Dönerci Şahin Usta
items.description: A no-frills döner spot near the Grand Bazaar beloved by traders and locals for decades. Thin-sliced lamb on fresh bread.

items.name: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi
items.description: One of Istanbul's most famous köfte restaurants, operating since 1920. Simple, perfect, unpretentious.
items.tip: Order the köfte with white beans and bread. Ignore anything else on the menu — this is a one-dish institution.

items.name: Fatih Çarşamba Pazarı (Wednesday Market)
items.description: One of Istanbul's largest and most atmospheric weekly markets. Vegetables, spices, olives, cheeses — a proper sensory experience.
items.tip: Wednesday mornings only. Bring a bag and go early — it gets very crowded by midday.

items.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
items.description: Sinan's masterpiece and one of the most beautiful buildings in the world. The courtyard offers panoramic views of the Golden Horn. Far less crowded than the Blue Mosque.
items.tip: Visit at prayer time to hear the call to prayer echo through the courtyard — an unforgettable experience. Dress modestly.

items.name: Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı)
items.description: The world's oldest and largest covered market. 4,000 shops across 61 covered streets. Disorienting, magnificent, and unlike anywhere else.
items.tip: Go to browse, not necessarily to buy. Prices are high in tourist areas — for real purchases, head to the surrounding streets.

items.name: Theodosian Walls
items.description: The Byzantine city walls that protected Constantinople for over a thousand years. Largely intact and strikingly undervisited. Walk a section of the top.
items.tip: The section between Edirnekapı and Yedikule gates is the most photogenic. Best in the morning light.

items.name: Chora Church (Kariye Müzesi)
items.description: Byzantine mosaics and frescoes arguably more spectacular than Hagia Sophia — and far less visited. A genuine wonder.

tips: Fatih is one of the few areas of Istanbul where you can feel genuinely far from the tourist trail — especially north of the Grand Bazaar.
The neighbourhood is conservative — dress modestly and be respectful around mosques.
Tram T1 runs through the heart of Fatih (Sultanahmet stop) — the easiest way to arrive.
Explore the streets between the Grand Bazaar and Süleymaniye for the most authentic trading atmosphere in the city.
